A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same equilibrium-planner research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original VirtualHome-Env experiments, including planner performance, feedback ablations, computational analyses, and qualitative execution traces.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments and adds convergence measurements, controlled baseline comparisons, and further execution traces in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), Algorithm 1, the supervised equilibrium objective, nested refinement, equilibrium memory, and world-model feedback remain unchanged. Expanded descriptions of alternating training steps and feedback scheduling clarify the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same VirtualHome-Env household-planning coverage: 292 tasks, 1,360 trajectories, seven scenes, and three generalization subsets. The feedback conditions already appear in v3 Table 3. v5 Table 4 describes other works' dataset protocols without adopting them.

E2.justification: The main performance comparator set is retained. v5 adds unfinetuned Llama to the convergence comparison in Table 5, SELF-REFINE to the no-feedback comparison in Table 6, and world-model-equipped Tree-Planner variants with N=25 and N=50 in Table 7.

E3.justification: The primary splits, metrics, training epochs, and correction limit remain unchanged. Added evaluations introduce a convergence design using 60 random tasks and ten initial plans per task, alongside controlled comparisons supplying world-model feedback to Tree-Planner.

E4.justification: Appendix C substantially expands diagnostic evidence: convergence across initializations and model variants, no-feedback self-refinement comparisons, and Tree-Planner's response to world-model feedback. Figures 13–14 expose inner-loop behavior, while Figure 11 adds an email-task baseline comparison. The earlier feedback comparison is retained as Figure 12.

E5.justification: v5 Table 5 documents repeated initialization using ten initial plans for each of 60 tasks and reports convergence means, standard deviations, minima, and maxima. v3 already reports mean and standard deviation in Figure 6b. Neither version reports uncertainty intervals for the main performance tables.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 are numerically identical, and Figures 5–6 retain their results. Substantial supplementary results are added: Table 5 reports mean convergence iterations of 6.70, 2.46, and 3.02 for original Llama, supervised Llama, and ours; Table 6 adds SELF-REFINE's no-feedback scores; Table 7 adds Tree-Planner/world-model scores. Further qualitative traces are also reported.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly states contraction with Lipschitz constant below one as a sufficient fixed-point convergence condition and mentions a well-posedness relaxation. The existing implicit-function theorem, gradient derivation, and proof are retained, with the proof moved to A.4. No new planner-specific convergence guarantee is established.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: supervised training of self-refinement without additional verifiers or reward models, efficient nested feedback integration with equilibrium reuse, and strong VirtualHome-Env performance with inference-computation scaling. The additions support rather than redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v5 explicitly acknowledges inferior no-feedback performance against Tree-Planner and attributes it to refining one plan versus generating 25 or 50 candidates. It expands explanations of flexible feedback use and greedy-sampling convergence, qualifies the Jacobian approximation's theoretical support, and adds feasibility constraints around combining planning with large reasoning models.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 newly specifies the world model's Llama 3 8B Instruct initialization, training after planner completion, feedback-prediction data format, and approximately 30-hour training cost. Memory sampling and feedback alternation receive clearer descriptions. These are documentation additions; the existing hyperparameters, prompts, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1–A.3 substantially expands technical positioning through implicit differential-equation models, one-step gradient approximations, and Transformer-based equilibrium models, adding works such as Chen, Kidger, Bolte, and Choe. The introduction also incorporates DeepSeek-R1 and sharpens the comparison with reinforcement learning dependent on efficient verifiers.

P1.justification: Most main prose and the overall section sequence are retained, with localized language and explanation edits. v5 separates Visualization into Section 4.3, organizes the expanded appendix background and analyses into subsections, adds an Impact Statement, and revises author and publication text.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column preprint layout to a two-column conference layout, extensively resizing and relocating displays. v5 adds Tables 4–7 and Figures 11, 13, and 14, renumbers the earlier Figure 11 as Figure 12, and revises captions and backtracking annotations.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful controls separating self-refinement from world-model effects (Tables 6–7), convergence checks across initial plans (Table 5), and clearer world-model training documentation. Explicitly acknowledging Tree-Planner's no-feedback advantage improves interpretation. These targeted additions close specific validation and transparency gaps, yielding a limited but clear overall improvement.
